security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, localhost examples, mocks, and illustrative test code. The real risk is the with-server helper, which can execute arbitrary user-supplied commands and starts server strings with shell=True. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: with-server.py starts --server values with shell=True and no allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True. Accept argument arrays, predefined commands, or require explicit confirmation for the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: The helper runs arbitrary trailing commands from CLI arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict commands to expected test runners or show the exact command and working directory before running it.

remediation.issue: The skill tells users to invoke bundled scripts as black boxes.
remediation.suggestion: Change the guidance to inspect bundled scripts, run --help, and confirm command behavior before invocation.

remediation.issue: Examples write screenshots and console logs to fixed local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use user-selected output paths and warn that logs or screenshots may contain sensitive page data.

semantic_findings.title: Misleading Command Validation Claim
semantic_findings.description: scripts/with-server.py says the server command is "validated at parse time," but the code only parses arguments before shell=True execution. This can cause unsafe trust in user-supplied commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line before subprocess.Popen claims validation while the command is directly passed to shell=True. No validation logic is present in the surrounding code.

semantic_findings.title: Bundled Script Invoked As Black Box
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs users to "Use bundled scripts as black boxes" before invoking helper scripts. This discourages inspection of a helper that executes local commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit, and the cited helper contains both server and command execution. The risk is operational guidance, not a hidden payload.

content.value_statement: Building reliable tests across stacks is hard when teams mix TDD, coverage goals, and browser automation. This skill gives structured testing workflows, Playwright patterns, and report templates for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Designs unit, integration, and end-to-end test strategies.
Guides red, green, refactor workflows for TDD.
Provides framework-specific examples for pytest, Jest, Vitest, JUnit, Go, and Rust.
Explains Playwright browser testing patterns for dynamic web applications.
Suggests coverage goals, quality gates, and CI pipeline placement.
Includes a test quality report template for audit summaries.
limitations: It does not run tests unless the agent executes project commands.
Framework advice may need adjustment for custom project conventions.
Playwright examples assume local development servers and basic browser setup.
Coverage targets are guidance, not proof of defect-free code.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Test Suite
use_cases.description: Create a balanced unit, integration, and end-to-end plan before a new feature reaches production.

use_cases.title: Practice TDD on Feature Work
use_cases.description: Write one failing test, implement the smallest change, then refactor while preserving coverage.

use_cases.title: Check Web App Behavior
use_cases.description: Use Playwright patterns to inspect rendered pages, choose selectors, and verify user flows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a feature or service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test plan for this feature. Include unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage, with the most important edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Write Focused Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate test authoring for existing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write focused tests for this code using arrange, act, assert. Cover happy paths, errors, and boundary cases.

prompt_templates.title: Apply TDD
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for building behavior test first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through TDD for this behavior. Start with one failing test, then propose the smallest implementation and refactor step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Test Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a mature suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this test suite for coverage gaps, flaky patterns, slow tests, missing mocks, and CI quality gates. Return prioritized recommendations.

output_examples.input: Review my checkout tests for gaps.
output: Identifies missing payment failure, discount, and authorization checks.
Separates unit coverage from browser flow coverage.
Recommends a small set of high-value tests before release.

output_examples.input: Help me test a dynamic dashboard with Playwright.
output: Starts with page inspection and load-state guidance.
Recommends stable selectors for buttons, links, and inputs.
Suggests assertions for visible dashboard state after login.
Summarizes coverage, reliability risks, and test gaps.
Calls out flaky tests and slow pipeline stages.
Ranks remediation work by impact and urgency.

best_practices: Start with the smallest behavior that can fail, then grow coverage deliberately.
Keep tests independent, deterministic, and easy to run in local and CI environments.
Use mocks for external systems, but keep critical user flows covered by integration or E2E tests.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before defining the expected behavior in a test.
Using broad browser tests for logic that a fast unit test can verify.
Trusting coverage percentage without checking important branches and failure paths.

faq.question: Does this skill support TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the red, green, refactor cycle and how to apply it one behavior at a time.

faq.question: Can it help with Playwright tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for local web app testing, selector discovery, screenshots, console logs, and browser cleanup.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: It includes examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, and Rust testing workflows.

faq.question: Does it execute tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples. Execution depends on the agent and the commands the user approves.

faq.question: Can it improve CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests where unit, integration, end-to-end, coverage, and performance checks fit in CI.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It can also audit existing suites, identify gaps, and recommend focused improvements.
